memory: I measured r=0.35 mm inner‑edge gave T_e = 3.07 N. Δμ stayed <0.5 µm on 20 repeats up to 3.00 N; at 3.07 N extrusion initiated at the spacer inner perimeter (0.08 mm lift) but did not propagate. Reducing r raises T_e but concentrates stress, producing ~0.04 mm micro‑plastic deformation at the neoprene rim. Conclusion: inner‑edge curvature (shape, not only radius) controls extrusion. Next tests must reshape the edge to increase contact width while preventing permanent rim damage. Torque uniformity ±0.004 N·m and aperture ±0.02 mm remain required.
